summary: Request: Configure distinct quota refill intervals for background batch workers vs real-time sessions
description:
Issue summary: Customer asks whether Redwood can support different refill intervals (token refill cadence) for two distinct traffic classes: low-latency real-time sessions (SSE/websocket) and large background batch workers that run hourly backfills. Impact: Customer sees recurring 429s for background jobs at hour boundaries even when interactive sessions remain healthy; they want to avoid background jobs starving interactive traffic while also allowing background jobs to use a separate, slower refill pool.

Environment: Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-42) in us-east, production workload mixes short-lived SSE sessions (avg duration 45s, ~120 concurrent) and hourly batch workers that submit large multipart embed jobs (~20k tokens per job).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Schedule 40 batch workers to start exactly at the top of the hour, each submitting a multipart embed flow that consumes ~15k tokens.
2) During the same window, open 100 concurrent SSE-based interactive sessions from end-users.
3) Observe increased 429s for batch workers and occasional soft 429s for a subset of interactive sessions.

Expected behavior: Background jobs should draw from a separate refill cadence or burst pool so interactive sessions are prioritized and remain low-latency; background jobs may be rate-limited but should not cause client-facing sessions to degrade.

Actual behavior: Both traffic classes are accounting against the same tenant refill window, causing sawtooth 429 spikes at scheduled backfill times and contention for token buckets. Console shows token window depletion spikes at 00:00 UTC each hour.

Logs/dashboards referenced: token-window-heatmap (console), quota-service refill logs (linked), stacktrace snippets for 429 responses included in comments.

Customer request: Can Redwood configure separate refill intervals or isolated burst pools (e.g., long-lived SSE pool with 1s refill, background batch pool with 1h refill) on a per-route or per-priority-class basis for dedicated customers? If not, what guidance exists to mitigate 429s from scheduled batch spikes (recommended stagger, separate API keys, priority lanes, or dedicated burst pools)?

Two mitigation paths: 1) create route-level priority lanes with separate quota pools on Dedicated (requires config change + applied rollout) or 2) advise separate API keys mapped to different refill buckets (workaround). Checking quota-service code paths and whether per-route refill intervals are currently supported; filing INT ticket if infra change required.

2026-03-13 11:12 - Engineering (Investigator - Priya Singh): Confirmed current dedicated quota model supports per-route weighting but not independent refill intervals. Weighting reduces token drain but still shares same refill epoch. Splitting by API key creates separate tenant sub-quotas which can be used to approximate isolated pools. Investigating risk/behavior on console and billing side.

2026-03-14 08:30 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer asked for concrete steps to test the separate-key workaround. Proposed: generate two API keys via Console (interact-key, batch-key), map batch-key to lower priority class with slower refill via dedicated config (if supported) or enforce throttling client-side. Requested SRE to validate whether issuing a second key will create an isolated refill window in our quota service for this dedicated customer.

2026-03-14 12:05 - NovaAnalytics (Customer): We'll try key separation this week; please confirm if there are billing implications or per-key meter differences. Also requesting an engineered option for per-route refill intervals as a product feature request.
investigation_notes: Checked quota-service logs for customer-dedicated-42: refill epoch aligns to 00:00:00 UTC hourly causing simultaneous bucket replenishment and exhaustion patterns.
Console token-window-heatmap snapshot shows sharp drops at hour boundaries correlated with batch job starts (see console link).
Per-route weights are applied but do not create separate refill epochs — weight only scales allocation each refill event.

Creating a separate API key appears to create an independent API-key-level accounting path which can be used to split burst accounting; need to confirm whether sub-quotas are isolated from tenant-level caps in billing and SLA calculations.

Risk: splitting keys without adjusting priority may still allow combined tenant cap enforcement to produce 429s if tenant cap is reached; recommended approach combines key-splitting + priority class isolation + staggered start times.
Related infra check: INT ticket suggested for adding per-route refill interval feature (INT-404210 placeholder).
next_steps: Support: Provide step-by-step runbook to customer for creating separate API keys and configuring route weights in Console.
SRE: Validate in staging whether issuing multiple API keys under the dedicated tenant creates independent refill windows; report back with test traces and quota logs (target: 2026-03-16).
Product: Capture feature request for per-priority/route refill cadence with customer impact notes; include in roadmap backlog if repeated asks observed.
Customer: Attempt separate-key test and provide new traces for 429s after segregation; optionally stagger batch job starts by 5-10 minutes as temporary mitigation.
business_impact: Customer's hourly backfills are critical for analytics freshness; repeated 429s cause job failures and manual retries, increasing operational cost. Interactive sessions must remain low-latency for end-user SLAs.
workaround_advice: Short-term: create a dedicated API key for background workers and reduce their request concurrency; stagger job start times; enable lower weight for batch route. Long-term: product-level support for isolated refill intervals or dedicated burst pools per priority class.
